scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The August-September dispute surge is mainly a ticket-handling/response-capacity problem; faster or automated ticket answering (not a bill-accuracy fix) would bring volume back to baseline.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced incorrect bill calculations/estimate substitutions, directly causing the dispute surge.

H-AMI-GAP.statement: A vendor-side MDMS/AMI read delivery failure (incomplete or late AMI register reads) around August caused more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Manual meter-read collection or the field-to-billing handoff degraded around August (missed reads, bad uploads), increasing estimate substitutions and disputes.

H-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Field reading staffing shortfalls (as asserted by SH-FIELD) are the underlying cause of missed/late manual reads driving the dispute surge.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution even when a valid AMI read was received and exported before cutoff.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of disputed bills, 1785 had an ACTUAL read and 1240 had an ESTIMATED read — the majority of disputes are on bills where a real read was used, not on estimate-substituted bills. This means estimate-substitution (from AMI or field-read gaps) can at most explain the smaller 1240-record share of the dispute population; something else is driving disputes on correctly-read bills.

The observation still holds: 1785 disputed bills had ACTUAL reads and 1240 had ESTIMATED reads. It no longer supports treating the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes as a distinct cause-chain driven by estimate-substitution/route-completion gap: E-11 shows 95.5% of that 1240 is actually the same import-rejection-of-valid-AMI-read mechanism already implicated in the ACTUAL-read disputes, so the premise of two parallel causes (rule-change for ACTUAL reads, separate estimate-substitution gap for ESTIMATED reads) is wrong.

The billing-db tariff change log shows zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes were recorded in the system around the dispute period. This rules out a tariff-rate change as a cause of wrong bills, but does not speak to read-type estimate substitution, import validation rules, or ticket response capacity.

Field route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 88% against a 95% target across 9200 manual-read accounts, showing a real manual meter-read shortfall during the dispute-surge window. This confirms a route-completion gap exists but, taken alongside E-01, leaves open whether it is large enough to be the dominant driver of disputes.

The observation still holds: field route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 88% against a 95% target across 9200 manual-read accounts, confirming a real manual meter-read shortfall. It no longer supports the premise that this route-completion gap is a secondary driver of the ESTIMATED-read disputes, since E-11 shows 95.5% of those 1240 disputes stem from valid AMI reads being rejected at import for high consumption (not from missed/late manual reads), leaving at most the 4.5% NO_READ_RECEIVED cases as a candidate for any route-completion linkage.

crm-tickets dispute_response_times shows a median response of 1.6 days and p90 of 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, i.e. ticket handling is comfortably inside SLA for the large majority of tickets. This weighs against ticket-response slowness being the surge driver, since response capacity does not appear degraded.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly confirms the dispute surge in magnitude and timing: tickets rose from 610/590 in Jun/Jul 2026 to 1180/1260 in Aug/Sep 2026, roughly doubling as the initial request claimed. It establishes that a real volume surge occurred starting August but says nothing about what caused the wrong bills or disputes.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims field reading has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those customers to receive estimated bills. This is a self-reported, non-authoritative stakeholder claim offering a candidate explanation for the route-completion gap already observed in E-03, not independently verified against staffing or route records.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that no tariff change occurred this year is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that corroborates the already-recorded authoritative billing-db tariff_change_log result (E-02, 0 records). It adds no new verified information beyond what E-02 already established and does not speak to read-type estimate substitution, import rules, or ticket response capacity.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is an authoritative document (service contract §4.2) stating ORG-UTIL may request route priority changes but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager. This corroborates the existing K-DISPATCH constraint's authority structure for the push_route_update protected action on field-dispatch; it does not speak to the cause of the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log lagging_routes returned 14 distinct routes each with a completion value (sample: route R-00 at 0.70), giving a per-route breakdown of the aggregate 88% completion shortfall already recorded in E-03. The record contains only 'completion' and 'route' fields — no staffing/roster data — so it confirms the route-completion gap is spread across multiple routes but cannot test whether staffing shortage (E-06/CL-02) is the cause.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI reports that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today under vendor ticket TX-4471. As a non-authoritative stakeholder message it does not itself prove the mdms-export tool is now usable, but it indicates the previously ACCESS_PENDING blocker on the read_events_for_disputed_estimated query may now be resolvable and worth re-attempting.

mdms-export's read_events_for_disputed_estimated query shows that of the 1240 disputed bills with ESTIMATED reads (E-01), 1184 (95.5%) had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but were rejected at import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 (4.5%) show NO_READ_RECEIVED. This indicates the dominant driver of estimate substitution in this population is a billing-import validation rule rejecting high-consumption AMI reads, not AMI vendor delivery failure or field manual-read gaps, aligning the ESTIMATED-read disputes with the same rule-change mechanism already implicated in the ACTUAL-read disputes.

U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.question: Does the billing import validation rule-change log (DA-RULES / billing-config) show an actual rule change around August 2026 that explains incorrect calculations on ACTUAL-read bills?
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.decision_impact: If no rule change is found, H-RULE-CHANGE is falsified and the solution must pivot away from a billing-config remediation toward estimate-substitution/handoff causes.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.resolution_path: Query billing-config DA-RULES rule-change log for entries dated around August 2026 and compare timing/content against the H-RULE-CHANGE premise.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.safe_placeholder: Do not deploy any billing-rule-change remediation; report dispute-volume and estimate-share metrics only, and treat H-RULE-CHANGE as unconfirmed, until the log is checked.

U-MDMS-ACCESS-BLOCKED.question: Is AMI/MDMS read-event data (needed to test H-AMI-GAP) obtainable, given mdms-export is DEGRADED and vendor access is ACCESS_PENDING with no fallback path (recent HOLD, seq 96)?
U-MDMS-ACCESS-BLOCKED.decision_impact: Without MDMS data, H-AMI-GAP cannot be tested and the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes cannot be attributed between AMI delivery failure and field-read gaps.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-BLOCKED.resolution_path: Follow up with ORG-AMI vendor to provision mdms-export access; retry once tool_health moves off DEGRADED/ACCESS_PENDING.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-BLOCKED.safe_placeholder: Proceed without AMI read-event data; report the ESTIMATED-read share (M-DISPUTED-BILL-ESTIMATE-SHARE) without attributing it to AMI vs field causes until vendor access is restored.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-BLOCKED.resolution: E-11 is an AUTHORITATIVE, COMPLETE mdms-export query result, confirming mdms-export access is now available and AMI/MDMS read-event data is obtainable, resolving the prior ACCESS_PENDING blocker.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-VERIFIC.question: Is SH-FIELD's self-reported staffing shortage (E-06, non-authoritative) actually the cause of the route-completion gap (E-03), or is there another operational cause?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-VERIFIC.decision_impact: If the staffing claim is unverified or wrong, a route-priority fix would not address the real cause of the route-completion gap.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-VERIFIC.resolution_path: Cross-check SH-FIELD's staffing claim (E-06) against ORG-FIELD staffing/route records in DA-ROUTE for the Jul-Sep 2026 period.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-VERIFIC.safe_placeholder: Treat the staffing shortage as an unverified contributing factor; do not base any route-priority change solely on E-06 without route-log corroboration.

U-ESTIMATE-SHARE-ATTRIBUTION.question: What specifically drives the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes - AMI delivery gaps, field-read/handoff gaps, or both - and in what proportion?
U-ESTIMATE-SHARE-ATTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation should target AMI vendor delivery, field read collection, or both for the ESTIMATED-read disputes.
U-ESTIMATE-SHARE-ATTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Compare MDMS read-event completeness (once accessible) against field route-completion gaps for the same accounts/period.
U-ESTIMATE-SHARE-ATTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Report the ESTIMATED-read share as a single aggregate figure without an AMI/field split until both data sources are available.
U-ESTIMATE-SHARE-ATTRIBUTION.resolution: E-11 shows 1184/1240 (95.5%) disputed-estimated bills had an AMI read received/exported but import-rejected for high consumption, versus 56/1240 (4.5%) with no AMI read received — attributing the large majority to billing-import rejection rather than AMI delivery gaps or field-read gaps.

U-HANDOFF-FIELD-BILL-VALIDITY.question: Was the H-FIELD-BILL manual-read handoff (ORG-FIELD to ORG-UTIL) delivered and semantically valid during Aug-Sep 2026, or did a delivery/parsing gap itself contribute to estimate substitution?
U-HANDOFF-FIELD-BILL-VALIDITY.decision_impact: A degraded handoff would explain part of the route-completion-linked dispute share independent of staffing, changing what verify_field_staffing_claim should check.
U-HANDOFF-FIELD-BILL-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Inspect H-FIELD-BILL daily-upload delivery logs and record counts against expected manual-read volumes for Aug-Sep 2026.
U-HANDOFF-FIELD-BILL-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat manual-read data feeding DA-ROUTE/DA-BILL as unverified for delivery completeness; do not rule out a handoff-level cause when verifying the staffing claim.

U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.question: Was the H-MDMS-BILL nightly AMI-register-read export (ORG-AMI to ORG-UTIL) delivered and semantically valid during Aug-Sep 2026?
U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.decision_impact: An invalid or incomplete MDMS-to-billing handoff, separate from vendor read-access being blocked, could itself drive estimate substitution tested under H-AMI-GAP.
U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Once mdms-export access is granted, check H-MDMS-BILL delivery timestamps/record counts against billing import logs for Aug-Sep 2026.
U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Do not assume the nightly AMI export was complete; treat any AMI-based estimate-substitution conclusions as provisional until this handoff is confirmed.
